free_text: The patient is a 77-year-old male with a PSA of 6.0 and a biopsy-proven Gleason 4+3 carcinoma (ISUP grade group 2) with perineural invasion. MRI demonstrated a PI-RADS 4 lesion with restricted diffusion. Given the established cancer and patient age, individual treatment benefit and preferences require clinical review. The trade-off involves balancing potential oncologic control against the risks associated with treatment in an elderly patient with comorbidities.
